```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Smit_2019_gentamicin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Smit_2019_gentamicin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-019-00762-4> (open access, PMC6768900)

Smit et al. gave a single intravenous gentamicin dose to 20 morbidly obese
adults scheduled for bariatric surgery and 8 non-obese healthy volunteers,
sampled each for 24 h, and fitted a two-compartment model in NONMEM 7.3. Total
body weight (TBW) was the best size descriptor for both clearance (exponent
0.729) and central volume (exponent 1.25). The authors then simulated
alternative dosing regimens across 50-215 kg and proposed a nomogram based on
a "dose weight" of 70 x (TBW/70)^0.73 (Table 3).

# Population

```{r population}
mod <- readModelDb("Smit_2019_gentamicin")
str(mod()$population)
```

Table 1 of the paper lists the baseline characteristics. The 20 morbidly
obese participants (50% male) had a median TBW of 148.8 kg (range 109-221),
lean body weight (LBW, Janmahasatian) 76.5 kg, BMI 44.4 kg/m^2 and age 40.5
years; the 8 non-obese volunteers (50% male) had a median TBW of 72.9 kg
(53-86), BMI 21.8 kg/m^2 and age 22.0 years. All had an eGFR above 60 mL/min;
the measured 24-h urine GFR was 110-230 mL/min in the obese group. The obese
participants received 5 mg/kg LBW and the non-obese 5 mg/kg TBW, each as a
30-min infusion (median dose 380 and 360 mg).

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Smit_2019_gentamicin.R`. The table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL at 70 kg) | log(0.0892 L/min) | Table 2, final model, CL70kg; Eq. 5 |
| `lvc` (Vc at 70 kg) | log(11.9 L) | Table 2, final model, Vc70kg; Eq. 4 |
| `lq` (Q) | log(0.0848 L/min) | Table 2, final model |
| `lvp` (Vp) | log(7.29 L) | Table 2, final model |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.729 | Table 2, Z (exponent on TBW/70 for CL) |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1.25 | Table 2, X (exponent on TBW/70 for Vc) |
| `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.181^2) | Table 2, IIV CL 18.1% |
| `etalvc` | log(1 + 0.192^2) | Table 2, IIV Vc 19.2% |
| covariance `etalcl`-`etalvc` | 0.0316 | Table 2, covariance IIV Vc-CL |
| `propSd` | 0.159 | Table 2, proportional error (footnote b: SD) |
| `addSd` | 0.206 mg/L | Table 2, additive error (footnote b: SD) |
| `cl = CL70kg * (WT/70)^Z`, `vc = Vc70kg * (WT/70)^X` | -- | Table 2 equations; Eqs. 4-5 |
| Two-compartment, IV infusion into `central` | -- | Results ("A two-compartment model ... best described the data"); ESM (ADVAN3) |
| Log-normal IIV, `theta_i = theta * exp(eta_i)` | -- | ESM Eq. 1 |
| `Cc ~ add(addSd) + prop(propSd)` | -- | ESM Eq. 2, `Y = Cpred + Cpred * eps1 + eps2` |

# Typical-value covariate relationships (Figure 2)

```{r figure-2}
# Replicates the covariate lines of Figure 2 of Smit 2019.
wt_grid <- tibble(WT = seq(50, 225, by = 1)) |>
  mutate(
    `Vc (L)` = 11.9 * (WT / 70)^1.25,
    `CL (L/min)` = 0.0892 * (WT / 70)^0.729
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-WT, names_to = "parameter")
ggplot(wt_grid, aes(WT, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Total body weight (kg)", y = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the covariate lines of Figure 2 of Smit 2019."
  )
```

# Virtual cohort matching the study

The two study groups are rebuilt with 200 virtual participants each. TBW is
drawn to match the medians and ranges of Table 1; height (needed for LBW) is
not reported in the paper and is drawn from Dutch adult norms by sex.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2019)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)

# Janmahasatian 2005 lean body weight (the formula the paper used for dosing)
lbw_janma <- function(wt, ht_cm, male) {
  bmi <- wt / (ht_cm / 100)^2
  ifelse(
    male == 1,
    9270 * wt / (6680 + 216 * bmi),
    9270 * wt / (8780 + 244 * bmi)
  )
}

draw_trunc <- function(n, draw, lo, hi) {
  out <- draw(n)
  bad <- out < lo | out > hi
  while (any(bad)) {
    out[bad] <- draw(sum(bad))
    bad <- out < lo | out > hi
  }
  out
}

n_per_group <- 200
make_group <- function(grp, id_offset) {
  male <- rep(c(1, 0), length.out = n_per_group)
  wt <- if (grp == "Morbidly obese") {
    draw_trunc(n_per_group, function(n) rlnorm(n, log(148.8), 0.17), 109, 221)
  } else {
    draw_trunc(n_per_group, function(n) rnorm(n, 72.9, 9), 53, 86)
  }
  ht <- ifelse(male == 1, rnorm(n_per_group, 181, 7), rnorm(n_per_group, 168, 7))
  tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_per_group),
    group = grp,
    WT = wt,
    LBW = lbw_janma(wt, ht, male)
  ) |>
    mutate(dose = if (grp == "Morbidly obese") 5 * LBW else 5 * WT)
}
subjects <- bind_rows(
  make_group("Morbidly obese", 0L),
  make_group("Non-obese", n_per_group)
)

subjects |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    `TBW median (kg)` = median(WT),
    `LBW median (kg)` = median(LBW),
    `Dose median (mg)` = median(dose),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohort vs. Table 1 (obese: TBW 148.8, LBW 76.5, dose 380; non-obese: TBW 72.9, dose 360).")

# Paper sampling times: 5, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 360, 720, 1440 min after
# the end of the 30-min infusion, plus a finer grid for plotting.
t_samp <- 0.5 + c(5, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 360, 720, 1440) / 60
t_obs <- sort(unique(c(0, seq(0.25, 24, by = 0.25), 1, t_samp)))
t_obs <- t_obs[t_obs <= 24]

dose_rows <- subjects |>
  transmute(id, group, WT, time = 0, amt = dose, rate = dose / 0.5, evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
obs_rows <- subjects |>
  select(id, group, WT) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = t_obs) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation (Figure 1 and Figure 3)

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("group")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-1}
# Replicates Figures 1 and 3 of Smit 2019: concentration-time profiles after a
# single 30-min infusion, by group (median and 2.5-97.5th percentiles of the
# individual predictions, without residual error).
sim |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(group, time) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(Cc, 0.025), med = median(Cc), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.4, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of infusion (h)", y = "Gentamicin (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figures 1 and 3 of Smit 2019 (dotted line: LLOQ 0.4 mg/L)."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports AUC24 by the trapezoidal rule, and defines Cmax as the
concentration 1 h after the start of infusion (Methods, Non-Compartmental
Statistical Analysis). The concentration declines monotonically after the
infusion ends at 0.5 h, so PKNCA's `cmax` over the interval 1-24 h is the
concentration at 1 h.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, group)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  events |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt, group),
  amt ~ time | group + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 1), end = c(24, 24),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE), cmax = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(
    (PPTESTCD == "auclast" & start == 0) | (PPTESTCD == "cmax" & start == 1)
  )
```

```{r nca-compare}
# Results text: AUC24 43.7 vs 68.7 mg*h/L and Cmax (1 h) 8.6 vs 17.8 mg/L.
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,           ~auclast, ~cmax,
  "Morbidly obese", 43.7,     8.6,
  "Non-obese",      68.7,     17.8
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_df,
  reference = published,
  by = "group",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L", cmax = "mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated (median) vs. published NCA. AUC0-last is AUC0-24; Cmax is the concentration 1 h after the start of infusion. * differs by > 20%."
)

med <- nca_df |>
  group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(
    published |> pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("group", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - ref) / ref)
# A mis-transcribed CL, Vc or exponent moves these medians by tens of percent.
stopifnot(all(abs(med$pct_diff) < 20))
```

All four medians fall within 20% of the published values. The morbidly obese
AUC24 runs about 10% low; most of that gap is dose, not clearance. The virtual
obese cohort's median LBW-based dose is about 6% below the study's 380 mg
(Table 1), because heights are not reported and are drawn from population
norms. Per milligram of dose the gap is about 5%.

# Dosing-regimen simulations (Figure 4 and Table 3)

The authors simulated six regimens over 50-215 kg using NHANES body-size data.
Here each regimen uses 200 virtual adults with TBW uniform over 50-215 kg,
half male, and height drawn from US adult norms by sex. Ideal body weight
uses the Devine formula and adjusted body weight is IBW + 0.4 x (TBW - IBW),
with IBW used when TBW < IBW (Methods, Eq. 1).

```{r regimens}
nomogram <- function(wt) {
  # Table 3: dose on TBW below 100 kg, then fixed doses per 20-kg band.
  case_when(
    wt < 100 ~ 5 * wt,
    wt < 120 ~ 480,
    wt < 140 ~ 560,
    wt < 160 ~ 600,
    wt < 180 ~ 680,
    wt < 200 ~ 760,
    TRUE ~ 800
  )
}
regimens <- c(
  "5 mg/kg TBW", "7 mg/kg TBW", "5 mg/kg LBW", "8 mg/kg LBW",
  "5 mg/kg ABW", "Nomogram (dose weight)"
)
n_reg <- 200
base <- tibble(
  WT = runif(n_reg, 50, 215),
  male = rep(c(1, 0), length.out = n_reg),
  HT = ifelse(male == 1, rnorm(n_reg, 175.7, 7.5), rnorm(n_reg, 162, 7))
) |>
  mutate(
    LBW = lbw_janma(WT, HT, male),
    IBW = ifelse(male == 1, 50, 45.5) + 2.3 * (HT / 2.54 - 60),
    ABW = ifelse(WT < IBW, IBW, IBW + 0.4 * (WT - IBW))
  )
reg_subjects <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(regimens), function(i) {
  base |>
    mutate(
      id = (i - 1L) * n_reg + seq_len(n_reg),
      regimen = regimens[i],
      dose = switch(regimens[i],
        "5 mg/kg TBW" = 5 * WT,
        "7 mg/kg TBW" = 7 * WT,
        "5 mg/kg LBW" = 5 * LBW,
        "8 mg/kg LBW" = 8 * LBW,
        "5 mg/kg ABW" = 5 * ABW,
        "Nomogram (dose weight)" = nomogram(WT)
      )
    )
}))
t_reg <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24)
reg_events <- bind_rows(
  reg_subjects |>
    transmute(id, regimen, WT, time = 0, amt = dose, rate = dose / 0.5, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  reg_subjects |>
    select(id, regimen, WT) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = t_reg) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(reg_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

reg_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = reg_events, keep = c("regimen")) |>
  as.data.frame()
reg_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
    reg_sim |> filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> select(id, time, Cc, regimen),
    Cc ~ time | regimen + id
  ),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
    reg_events |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt, regimen),
    amt ~ time | regimen + id
  ),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE)
))
reg_out <- as.data.frame(reg_nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, regimen, AUC24 = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(
    reg_sim |> filter(time == 24) |> select(id, Cmin = Cc),
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  left_join(reg_subjects |> select(id, WT), by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    band = cut(WT,
      breaks = c(50, 100, 120, 140, 160, 180, 200, 215),
      labels = c("50-100", "100-120", "120-140", "140-160", "160-180", "180-200", "200-215"),
      include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE
    ),
    regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens)
  )
target <- median(reg_out$AUC24[reg_out$regimen == "5 mg/kg TBW" & reg_out$WT < 100])
```

```{r figure-4, fig.height = 7}
# Replicates Figure 4 of Smit 2019: AUC24 (upper) and Cmin (lower) by weight band.
reg_out |>
  select(regimen, band, AUC24, Cmin) |>
  pivot_longer(c(AUC24, Cmin), names_to = "metric") |>
  ggplot(aes(band, value)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(
    data = tibble(metric = c("AUC24", "Cmin"), ref = c(target, 1)),
    aes(yintercept = ref), linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ regimen, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Total body weight (kg)", y = "AUC24 (mg*h/L) / Cmin (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Smit 2019 (dashed: AUC24 target from 5 mg/kg TBW < 100 kg; Cmin 1 mg/L)."
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, size = 6))
```

```{r regimen-checks}
reg_out |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    `AUC24 median (mg*h/L)` = median(AUC24),
    `AUC24 median, > 150 kg` = median(AUC24[WT > 150]),
    `Cmin median (mg/L)` = median(Cmin),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Regimen summary from the stochastic simulation.")

# The paper's conclusions, checked on the robust centre of each regimen:
# (1) every regimen keeps the median Cmin below 1 mg/L;
# (2) the dose-weight nomogram keeps AUC24 near the < 100 kg target above 150 kg.
reg_med <- reg_out |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(cmin = median(Cmin), auc_heavy = median(AUC24[WT > 150]), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(
  all(reg_med$cmin < 1),
  abs(reg_med$auc_heavy[reg_med$regimen == "Nomogram (dose weight)"] / target - 1) < 0.15
)
```

The dose weight follows from the clearance equation: a dose of
5 mg/kg x 70 x (TBW/70)^0.73 divided by CL70kg x (TBW/70)^0.729 is almost
independent of TBW. The typical-value check below confirms this on the
packaged model without random effects, and that LBW-based dosing loses
exposure as weight rises while TBW-based dosing gains it (Figure 4, upper
panel).

```{r typical-check}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
wts <- c(60, 100, 150, 215)
typ_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(wts), function(i) {
  wt <- wts[i]
  dw <- 70 * (wt / 70)^0.73
  lbw <- lbw_janma(wt, 175, 1)
  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      id = (i - 1) * 3 + 1:3, WT = wt,
      regimen = c("dose weight", "5 mg/kg TBW", "5 mg/kg LBW"),
      amt = c(5 * dw, 5 * wt, 5 * lbw)
    )
  )
})) |>
  mutate(time = 0, rate = amt / 0.5, evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
typ_obs <- typ_events |>
  select(id, WT, regimen) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 72, by = 0.05)) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
# zeroRe() leaves no omega, so rxode2 notes that a multi-subject solve has
# none; that note is expected and muffled.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
}
typ_sim <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod_typ,
    events = bind_rows(typ_events, typ_obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid)),
    keep = c("regimen")
  ),
  warning = muffle_no_omega
) |>
  as.data.frame()
typ_auc <- typ_sim |>
  group_by(id, regimen) |>
  summarise(
    WT = first(WT),
    # cumulative AUC to 72 h, then extrapolated with the terminal slope
    auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2) +
      last(Cc) / -coef(lm(log(Cc) ~ time, data = tail(pick(time, Cc), 100)))[[2]],
    cl = first(cl),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(typ_events |> select(id, amt), by = "id") |>
  mutate(auc_closed = amt / cl)
knitr::kable(typ_auc |> select(regimen, WT, amt, auc, auc_closed), digits = 2)
dw_auc <- typ_auc$auc_closed[typ_auc$regimen == "dose weight"]
tbw_auc <- typ_auc$auc_closed[typ_auc$regimen == "5 mg/kg TBW"]
lbw_auc <- typ_auc$auc_closed[typ_auc$regimen == "5 mg/kg LBW"]
stopifnot(
  # numerical integration of the solve agrees with dose / CL
  all(abs(typ_auc$auc / typ_auc$auc_closed - 1) < 0.01),
  # dose weight: exposure flat across 60-215 kg (exponent 0.73 vs 0.729)
  diff(range(dw_auc)) / mean(dw_auc) < 0.01,
  all(diff(tbw_auc) > 0),
  all(diff(lbw_auc) < 0)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- Table 2 prints IIV as a percentage. The supplementary methods define the
  etas as log-normal (`theta_i = theta * exp(eta_i)`), so the variances are
  `log(1 + CV^2)`. At 18-19% the alternative reading `CV^2` differs by under
  2%. The covariance 0.0316 is used as printed on the omega scale (implied
  correlation about 0.93).
- The Results text quotes the final-model IIV as 18.5% (Vc) and 17.4% (CL),
  slightly different from Table 2 (19.2% and 18.1%), probably from an
  intermediate covariate step; the Table 2 final-model values are used.
- The paper reports clearances in L/min. The model keeps the printed values in
  `ini()` and multiplies them by 60 in `model()`, so time is in hours.
- Below-LLOQ concentrations were fitted with the M3 method; this affects
  estimation only, not simulation.
- Heights are not reported. The study cohort uses Dutch adult heights
  (181 cm male, 168 cm female, SD 7 cm) to compute LBW for the obese dose; the
  regimen simulation uses US adult heights (175.7 and 162 cm) in place of the
  NHANES resampling the authors used, and draws TBW uniformly over 50-215 kg.
  The weight bands of Figure 4 are not stated in the text; the Table 3 bands
  are used.
- The 1-h and 24-h concentrations are compared as simulated without residual
  error, so they are model predictions rather than replicate observations.
- No correction notice for this article was found in the PMC record as of
  2026-11-25.
